articles.title: Week 3 Waiver-Wire Pickups and Sleepers Available in Majority of Fantasy Leagues
articles.summary: Week 3 got underway on Thursday night, and some fantasy managers may already be scrambling to play catch-up. Unfortunately, they may find that not every star draft pick is available, as injuries have already become a bit of a problem in 2026.
articles.body:
Week 3 got underway on Thursday night, and some fantasy managers may already be scrambling to play catch-up. Unfortunately, they may find that not every star draft pick is available, as injuries have already become a bit of a problem in 2026.

The good news is that some viable fill-ins may still be available on the waiver wire. Waiver claims have been processed in most leagues, but the following players aren't heavily rostered heading into the weekend.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring. Scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

With quarterbacks Jayden Daniels, Caleb Williams, Sam Darnold, and Jaxson Dart getting injured over the first two weeks, some managers may already be desperate for quarterback help. This week, they may be able to get it from New York Jets signal-caller Geno Smith.

Smith should not be viewed as a high-end season-long fantasy option. He's thrown for just 462 yards and one touchdown, and there's no guarantee that he'll keep rookie Cade Klubnik on the bench all season.

However, Smith has a terrific fantasy matchup this week against the Detroit Lions. New York will likely be playing from behind most of the game, and the Lions have surrendered more fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks than any other team this season.

Smith is only rostered in eight percent of fantasy leagues.

Kansas City Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson is a fifth-round rookie out of Nebraska. While he's no threat to unseat prized free-agent addition Kenneth Walker III as Kansas City's starter, it's clear that the Chiefs plan to use both backs this season.

Johnson has logged four receptions, 14 total touches, and 103 scrimmage yards this season.

While Johnson will remain a matchup-based flex play for the foreseeable future, he has a terrific matchup this week. The Chiefs will visit the Miami Dolphins, who have surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing running backs.

There's also a very good chance that the Chiefs will get up big on the Dolphins early and look to grind out the game on the ground. In that scenario, Johnson should see a sizeable workload. He's rostered in 26 percent of leagues.

Dontayvion Wicks, WR, Philadelphia Eagles

Following the Philadelphia Eagles' trade of A.J. Brown, most expected rookie Makai Lemon to quickly emerge as the team's No. 2 receiver behind DeVonta Smith. However, it's been trade acquisition Dontayvion Wicks in that role thus far.

Wicks ranks second on the team with seven catches and 147 receiving yards. He's also tied for second with one touchdown. He's seen no fewer than four targets in a game, and his role could grow with tight end Dallas Goedert battling an MCL sprain.

This week, Wicks probably doesn't have the highest ceiling, as the Chicago Bears are expected to be without their top two quarterbacks. If Chicago struggles to keep pace on the scoreboard, Jalen Hurts is unlikely to spend the game in pass-first mode. However, Wicks' floor as a flex option is solid, and he has a good amount of long-term upside.

Wicks is rostered in 32 percent of fantasy leagues.

Oronde Gadsden II, TE, Los Angeles Chargers

The Los Angeles Chargers' offense hasn't been very good in 2026, and it appears that Justin Herbert and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel are still trying to mesh. However, managers looking for a tight end should still consider Oronde Gadsden II.

Gadsden is likely to leap into a significant role for L.A. after the Chargers placed David Njoku on injured reserve. Fellow tight end Charlie Kolar is also dealing with a forearm injury.

While Gadsden has just four catches for 50 yards this season, he did find the end zone in Week 2, and he should see plenty of targets against the Buffalo Bills this week. Buffalo has looked like one of the league's top teams through two weeks, and the Chargers may have to pass often to keep pace.

Buffalo has surrendered the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends in 2026. Gadsden is rostered in 25 percent of leagues.

articles.title: Drake London Calls Michael Penix Jr. 'Definition of Resiliency' After Falcons' Upset of Packers
articles.summary: Michael Penix Jr. received high praise from Drake London after leading the Atlanta Falcons to an impressive 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers for their first victory of the season.
articles.body:
Michael Penix Jr. received high praise from Drake London after leading the Atlanta Falcons to an impressive 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers for their first victory of the season.

London told reporters after the game that Penix is the "definition of resiliency" as the third-year quarterback worked his way back from a torn ACL in his left knee.

Making his first start since Week 11 of the 2025 season, Penix had some rust coming out of the gate with an interception that ended Atlanta's first offensive possession.

Top takeaways from Thursday Night Football

Penix settled in after that to finish 18-of-25 for 256 yards with one touchdown and one interception. He helped the Falcons record season-highs in points, passing yards and total yards (498).

Even though there was no real question that Penix would return after injuring his knee last season, concerns about his viability only grew since it was the third time has torn his ACL.

The previous two times occurred in college and were to the ACL in his right knee, but there isn't a long history of NFL players returning and having success after having at least three ACL tears.

Former Carolina Panthers linebacker Thomas Davis Sr. is the most famous example of being able to do it. He tore the same ACL in three consecutive seasons from 2009 to '11 before returning to play nine additional seasons from 2012 to '20.

Penix's health and success is a huge storyline for the Falcons in 2026. He was a first-round pick two years ago and will become eligible for a contract extension after this season.

If Penix performs well, it will remove a huge question for Atlanta's front office to answer in the offseason as it looks to build up the roster.

There is a long way to go before getting to that point. Penix and the Falcons are currently focused on trying to play their way back into contention in what looks like a wide-open NFC South.

Next week is a marquee divisional showdown for the Falcons against the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome on Monday Night Football.

articles.title: Jets Hit the NFL Draft Jackpot After Devastating Packers Loss
articles.summary: The New York Jets have hit the 2027 NFL Draft jackpot after the Green Bay Packers' devastating loss to start Week 3. The post Jets Hit the NFL Draft Jackpot...
articles.body:
New York Jets fans probably still have a bitter taste in their mouths after letting one slip away in Week 2. Well, here's the antidote to your problems: the Green Bay Packers just lost 35-14 to the Atlanta Falcons to start Week 3.

"The Cowboys– Micah Parsons trade was an incredible deal from a surplus value standpoint by Jerry Jones. Unfortunately for Cowboys fans, the later Quinnen Williams trade had a horrible condition that will give a potential top 5 overall Packers 2027 first rounder away," Super Bowl-winning NFL Coach and Director of Analytics Ryan Paganetti posted on X.

Wait a second, who controls the Packers' first-rounder in the 2027 NFL Draft? Oh, that's right, that would be the Jets.

General manager Darren Mougey pulled off a masterclass move by negotiating a clause into the Quinnen Williams blockbuster trade to the Dallas Cowboys . The Jets will get whichever pick is better in the first round between the Cowboys and the Packers.

According to Tankathon , that would be the Packers selection, with the team dropping to 1-2. If the draft started today, they would have the 8th overall pick, which would be sent to the Jets.

When the Jets put that clause into the trade at the deadline last year, it didn't create many waves around the league because of the teams involved.

The Packers and the Cowboys are iconic NFL franchises that don't end up at the top of the draft very often.

Since 2006, the lowest win total the Packers have put up is six wins. They did that twice: 2008 and 2018. Since 2003, the lowest win total the Cowboys have put up is four wins. It happened once during an injury-riddled 2015 season.

However, that's why the moniker says any given Sunday. The NFL is a funny sport. Who knows which teams will be good and which teams will be bad on a year-to-year basis.

Mougey hit the jackpot with this trade. The Packers are 1-2; they should really be 0-3, but we don't have to get into that. Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur was asked after the latest loss to start Week 3 if he's considering firing coaches on his staff, and he refused to answer the question.

Things are going badly, and it could only get worse from here. According to ESPN , the Packers currently have the 8th easiest strength of schedule, yet they are 1-2. The games are only going to get tougher from here, which should be great news for the green and white.

Gang Green will only get one pick from either the Packers or the Cowboys. If the draft started today, they would get Green Bay's pick. They also hold their own first-rounder in 2027, but wait, there's more.

In the blockbuster Sauce Gardner trade, the Jets secured the Colts' first-rounder in the 2027 NFL Draft as well.

If the draft started today, the Jets would land the No. 3 overall pick because of the Colts ' 0-2 start to the season, per Tankathon .

"After the Indianapolis Colts' overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football, cornerback Sauce Gardner has not tasted victory on American soil in nearly two years. Gardner hasn't been on the winning side in the United States since a Dec. 2024 victory with the New York Jets, extending his personal losing streak to a whopping 644 days. During that span, his only winning experience was a victory by the Colts in the 2025 Berlin Game," Doric Sam of Bleacher Report wrote.

"Gardner endured a 0-7 start to the 2025 season with the Jets and sat out their first win in Week 8 against the Cincinnati Bengals . He was sent to the Colts at the Nov. 4 trade deadline, and his new team ended the year on a seven-game losing streak after defeating the Atlanta Falcons in Germany," Sam revealed.

The Jets have two big horses in the 2027 NFL Draft. Draft expert Trevor Sikkema told me on "Boy Green Daily" before the season that this 2027 class has a chance to be one of the best in a long time. That should be music to Jets fans' ears everywhere.

articles.title: Packers’ Week 3 blowout loss to Falcons has 2x Super Bowl champ ringing alarm bells
articles.summary: Damien Woody warns the Packers face serious issues.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers suffered another heavy defeat Thursday, losing 35-14 to the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field.

The loss dropped Green Bay to 1-2 after three weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Atlanta also improved to 1-2 after controlling the game from the second quarter.

Damien Woody, who won two Super Bowl championships as an offensive lineman with the New England Patriots , thinks the Packers have serious problems across both sides of the line. Speaking on the NFL on CBS broadcast, he delivered a blunt assessment.

"They're in trouble," Woody said, per NFL on CBS on X . "Oh, the Green Bay Packers are in trouble."

Woody pointed directly at Green Bay's inability to establish the line of scrimmage. The Packers finished with only 17 rushing yards on nine carries.

"First of all, up front, they can't run the football," Woody said. "That's the most evident thing about the Green Bay Packers."

The lack of rushing production placed additional pressure on quarterback Jordan Love throughout the night. Atlanta eventually built enough pressure to disrupt Green Bay's offensive rhythm.

"The Green Bay Packers are in TROUBLE!" 😳 @damienwoody #Final pic.twitter.com/YbJHIGaIGB — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) September 25, 2026

"The Green Bay Packers are in TROUBLE!" 😳 @damienwoody #Final pic.twitter.com/YbJHIGaIGB

NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) September 25, 2026

The Packers also struggled to protect Love against an aggressive Falcons defense. Atlanta held the Packers to 328 total yards while producing 498 yards offensively.

"They can't protect the quarterback, and tonight, they got absolutely gashed by the Atlanta Falcons ' rushing attack," Woody said.

Packers face bigger questions after Atlanta collapse

Glendale, Arizona, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

NFL Network's Michael Robinson identified another issue involving Atlanta's defensive approach. He said defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich's pressure looks appeared designed to speed up Love's decision-making.

"If you make Jordan Love think that he's going to get pressure, you're going to already speed up his process," Robinson said, per NFL Network on X . "Then you get the mistakes."

Atlanta rushed for 242 yards, with Bijan Robinson producing 194 yards and two touchdowns. Receiver Drake London added 194 yards as the Falcons repeatedly created explosive plays.

Robinson also questioned how Green Bay will function without Josh Jacobs, who remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The veteran running back's absence left the Packers without their primary rushing threat.

"This offense very badly needs a difference-maker at the running back position," Robinson said. "You can't have the play-action explosives if the guy behind you ain't there."

"This offense, very badly needs a difference maker at the running back position." — @RealMikeRob on his concern for the Packers after their loss to the Falcons. pic.twitter.com/ZmgsGh9eJa — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) September 25, 2026

"This offense, very badly needs a difference maker at the running back position." — @RealMikeRob on his concern for the Packers after their loss to the Falcons. pic.twitter.com/ZmgsGh9eJa

NFL Network (@nflnetwork) September 25, 2026

The Packers next face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road on Oct. 4. Green Bay must improve its rushing attack and protection before that matchup.

As Woody summarized, the problems extend beyond one position. "If you can't capture the line of scrimmage on either side of the ball, you're going to be in big trouble."

articles.title: NFL Exec Says 'Every Team' Looks for Edge with Social Media Videos After Mike Macdonald's Comments
articles.summary: Multiple NFL coaches and executives shrugged off Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald's admitted use of social media videos in scouting, noting that it is commonplace in the league.
articles.body:
Multiple NFL coaches and executives shrugged off Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald's admitted use of social media videos in scouting, noting that it is commonplace in the league.

Speaking to Jeff Howe of The Athletic, an anonymous high-ranking team executive called the situation a "nothing burger," adding, "Every team does it."

An anonymous coach agreed, saying, "It's very common. We all do it. Everyone does."

Top takeaways from Thursday Night Football

Meanwhile, an anonymous general manager called the controversy "absolutely nothing" and "a waste of time."

Earlier this week, a clip went public from Macdonald's appearance on In Depth With Graham Bensinger (h/t ESPN's Brady Henderson ), and in it, Macdonald admitted to using clips of training camp practices posted by fans on social media in order to scout the Denver Broncos prior to their 2024 regular-season opener.

"Fans will post plays from training camp on Twitter, so it's like public knowledge," Macdonald said. "We took like 100 plays from their training camp. We were scouting them."

Macdonald noted that Broncos head coach Sean Payton was initially furious about the tactics after finding out about them, going so far as to contact Seahawks general manager John Schneider.

"He got wind of it and he lost it," Macdonald said. "This is the middle of the season, and we won the game. We were in the fight our first year. There was a lot of s--t going on. So, he called John. He basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriot Spygate type of thing.

"I'm sitting there like, 'Oh my god. We didn't cheat.' They thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant and the whole thing. So, we had to counter with him and say, 'If you come out with this, we're going to sue you because it's not true.'"

One day after the story began making the rounds, Macdonald told reporters he apologized to Payton for it becoming public.

Payton then told reporters he has "a ton of respect for" Macdonald, adding, "He and I are good. Lord knows I've been in his position, you know, you're talking about something. The story is about three years ago."

Macdonald has enjoyed enormous success during his time as the Seahawks' head coach, posting a 26-10 record over parts of three seasons.

After narrowly missing the playoffs with a 10-7 record in his debut season, Macdonald led Seattle to a Super Bowl win last season.

The Seahawks are off to a 2-0 start early in the 2026 campaign, and they look like a threat to make another deep playoff run.

articles.title: NFL gameday: Brock Purdy 'in prime' for San Francisco 49ers, Patrick Mahomes chases Tom Brady record and Dexter Lawrence leads Cincinnati Bengals Super Bowl charge

articles.body:
He entered the league devoid of pressure or projections as Mr Irrelevant. Not long after he was tasked with leading perennial Super Bowl contention for the 49ers. Football onlookers have since been fiercely divided on where he stands among the NFL's premier quarterbacks. Was it the Kyle Shanahan system and the star-studded cast? Or is he just good? It is allowed to be both.

It comes with the asterisk of premature two-week conclusions territory, but Purdy is playing as well as any quarterback in football right now.

He enters week three with the highest completion percentage in the league at 80.4 having completed 45 of 56 passes for 492 yards and five touchdowns at 8.8 yards per attempt.

"We're starting to witness Brock's prime, and I think it's going to be a sight to behold," said 49ers offensive tackle Trent Williams.

"I've always loved Brock, but I think he's starting to get his respect now. He doesn't even relish in it. It's all about next week, going 1-0, and that's why he's a great leader."

Purdy doesn't earn acclaim for being one of the league's most athletic or dynamic out-of-structure two-way killers, but instead thrives on high-level processing, field diagnosis, anticipation and accuracy. It should also be said he is a far better scrambler than he gets credit for.

The best of what Purdy represents came in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins on a precision-perfect strike to Mike Evans, the 49ers quarterback moving one defender with a pump-fake before sliding left and threading a stunning off-platform bullet to his new wide receiver. Evans had run what began as a crossing route before momentarily adjusting into a corner break, Purdy picking him out with expert touch and timing to execute on a flood concept.

Twice Purdy has threatened one of the great underdog stories in NFL history. He famously guided the 49ers to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie after being selected with the 262nd and final pick of the Draft, only to suffer an elbow injury in the first quarter as Josh Johnson replaced him in a 31-7 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. He went one better the next season by taking San Francisco to Super Bowl LVIII, where they were beaten in overtime by the Kansas City Chiefs.

The system quarterback label has overshadowed him at times, while others have underlined his success in a scheme others have been unable to execute at such a high level. His 49ers have meanwhile been as unlucky with marquee injuries as any team in the league, as much hampering Shanahan's offense in recent years as they seek to work their way back to Super Bowl territory.

He now has a healthy Christian McCaffrey, a healthy George Kittle and, perhaps for the first time in his career, a proven elite veteran receiver in Mike Evans.

"I got really lucky," said Kittle on The Rich Eisen Show . "I get to play with Trent Williams right? We got him. Hall of Famer, plays like a Hall of Famer still. Mike Evans, Hall of Famer, plays like a Hall of Famer still.

"And so just when you add guys like that, it's just so much fun because every time we call a play and I know Mike has a chance of getting the ball, I'm like, 'this is so sick'. Brock Purdy's throwing the ball to Mike Evans and I'm blocking for him.

Purdy's 49ers look to go 3-0 this weekend when they take on the Arizona Cardinals, lead by one of Shanahan's disciples in first-year head coach Mike LaFleur.

Giants QB Jaxson Dart is set to miss the remainder of the regular season after suffering a knee injury that requires surgery in Monday's loss to the Rams

Seahawks QB Sam Darnold was a full participant in Thursday's practice and could return to action from his glute injury against the Commanders on Sunday

Bears QB Caleb Williams did not practice on Thursday and is a doubt to face the Eagles on Monday night after suffering a hamstring injury against the Vikings in Week Two

He takes on a Chargers offensive line enduring a miserable start to the season.

The early signs have been positive in wins over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Houston Texans, through which Lawrence is PFF's highest-graded interior defensive lineman. He has single-handedly elevated Cincinnati's front as a multi-gap nightmare for offensive lineman.

Arizona Cardinals @ San Francisco 49ers - 9.05pm - LIVE on Sky Sports Football: Upton Stout is beginning to make a name for himself in a 49ers jersey. The second-year corner out of Western Kentucky was showered with praise by Raheem Morris as San Francisco's 'player of the game on defense' against Miami, the 49ers defensive coordinator turning to the 24-year-old as an explosive blitz weapon capable of reading plays quickly, making stops laterally and adding another downhill threat to his defense.

The Cowboys are currently averaging a third-most 117 yards on the ground and 4.5 yards per carry as they prepare to take on a two-headed ground monster in Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry, to the latter of whom Jesse Minter could return his focus after bizarrely drifting from the star running back in the second half of last weekend's defeat to the New Orleans Saints.

articles.title: To kick or receive? NFL coaches still haven't figured out the overtime coin toss
articles.summary: The NFL changed overtime to guarantee both teams a possession, but that created a new strategic puzzle.
articles.body:
Prior to overtime last Sunday night, with his team in jeopardy of starting a pivotal season with two straight losses, Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen contemplated one of the toughest choices in football.

He had to decide whether to kick or receive if the Colts won the coin toss.

Winning the overtime coin toss used to be cause for celebration under the NFL's previous rules. The receiving team gained the opportunity to secure victory without its opponent touching the ball if it scored a touchdown on its opening possession.

The optimal strategy is far murkier now that the NFL's overtime system guarantees both teams possession of the ball. Winning the coin toss now means choosing between taking the ball first to chase a potential possession advantage or playing defense first to know exactly how many points are required to win.

The presence of quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the opposing huddle influenced Steichen's decision to give the Kansas City Chiefs the ball to start Sunday's overtime. As Steichen told reporters after the game, "If we go first with it, Mahomes gets four downs going the other way, so we wanted to play defense there and know we had four downs."

Steichen's decision backfired on the Colts when both teams settled for field goals on their initial possessions of overtime and Mahomes took advantage of getting the ball a second time. Harrison Butker's game-clinching 40-yard field goal sent the Chiefs spilling onto the field in celebration and sparked renewed debate over how teams should approach winning the overtime coin toss.

It's difficult to draw meaningful conclusions from the results of recent overtime games because the sample size is too small. Twenty games have gone to overtime since the NFL adopted the new rules for the playoffs in March 2022 and then extended them to the regular season in 2025. The team that won the overtime coin toss has chosen to kick in 14 of those 20 games. And yet the team that received the ball first is 11-8-1 (57.5%).

A study published by a football-obsessed cardiologist in The Journal of Sports Analytics this past July offered some of the first mathematical insight into the optimal strategy for the NFL's kick-or-receive overtime coin toss dilemma. Using a Monte Carlo simulation to predict which strategy would prove advantageous over 100,000 NFL overtimes, author Dylan Goings found that electing to receive the ball first would produce a win rate of 53.14%.

"Coaches who choose to kick are trading a structural positioning advantage for informational clarity that, in our analysis, does not translate to improved outcomes," Goings concluded.

Goings told Yahoo Sports he took on the project in his spare time last January after he and some college buddies got into a spirited debate over whether the Chicago Bears were right to kick the ball to the Rams at the start of overtime in the divisional playoffs. The cardiologist could not let the argument go unresolved, especially not when his background in medical research, risk stratification and statistical analysis gave him the tools to find a definitive answer.

"It's just the type of person I am," Goings said with a laugh. "If you have an argument with a friend and you have a hunch that you're right, let's settle it.

"I had already written code to do a Monte Carlo analysis for something very similar. So with just a few tweaks I had something that's relevant to football fans."

The key limitation to a Monte Carlo simulation — an analysis that uses random guessing over and over to predict the possible outcomes of an event — is that the results are only as good as the assumptions and probabilities that the researcher feeds into the simulation. Goings combatted that before submitting his study for publication by posting the results of his Monte Carlo simulation to a handful of Reddit forums and incorporating feedback on how heavily to weigh variables like two-point conversion strategy or clock pressure.

"It was like a peer review process from strangers on the internet," Goings said.

To test whether the optimal strategy varied if one team had an elite defense or a turnover-prone quarterback or a shaky kicker, Goings conducted a sensitivity analysis using extreme or even unrealistic efficiencies. There was no combination of variables, he said, where he found it was more advantageous to kick than to receive.

The best way for the team that has the ball second in overtime to eat into its disadvantage, according to Goings, is to aggressively go for the win on its initial possession. Whether by going for it on 4th-and-short instead of kicking a tying field goal or attempting a two-point conversion instead of kicking a tying extra point, those options are superior to matching scores and giving the opposing team possession of the ball in the sudden death format.

One of the most qualified people to assess Goings' findings might be a former backgammon world champion with a passion for game theory. Frank Frigo has worked with risk-averse NFL and college coaches to help them optimize their in-game decision making, first as a co-founder of data analysis firm EdjSports and now as an independent consultant.

When asked which strategy he favored for the overtime coin toss winner, Frigo told Yahoo Sports that he believes the potential to have a greater number of possessions by taking the ball first slightly outweighed the informational advantage of getting the ball second. Frigo hasn't run a full data simulation like Goings, but he pointed to data showing that 22.1% of NFL overtimes end on the third possession and 6.4% on the fifth.

"It's hard for me to imagine that the informational advantage of having the ball second outweighs that," Frigo said.

As fans in Buffalo know all too well, the NFL implemented its new overtime system in response to the Kansas City Chiefs beating the star-crossed Bills in the divisional round of the NFL playoffs in January 2022. After a thrilling, back-and-forth 60 minutes of regulation, the overtime coin flip had an outsize influence on the outcome. The Chiefs won the toss, and Mahomes promptly led them to a touchdown on the opening drive of overtime, stranding Josh Allen on the sideline with no way to respond, no way to impact the result.

The lack of debate over whether the kicking or receiving team has the advantage in overtime now is proof that the NFL's new system is working. Since the start of the 2025 regular season, the overtime coin toss winner has a record of 6-12-1. To this day, teams don't seem to fully understand how to capitalize on the slight structural advantage of receiving the ball first or how to negate much of the disadvantage of taking the ball second by playing for the win.

After his team lost 20-17 in overtime to the Green Bay Packers last Sunday, New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn struggled to explain to reporters why he elected to receive the ball first in overtime. Glenn said the Jets were hoping to eat most of the 10-minute clock with their opening drive, score a touchdown and put pressure on the Packers to answer.

"It didn't happen for us the way that I planned," Glenn conceded.

Later that night, Steichen also faced a barrage of questions about why he chose to kick a game-tying field goal at the end of the Colts' lone overtime possession rather than going for it on 4th-and-8 deep in Kansas City territory. Steichen initially sent his offense onto the field, only to gesture to quarterback Daniel Jones not to snap the ball.

"Had a play called, [but] had to love the look to run it there," Steichen said. "And, if not, obviously we took the delay of game there and kicked the field goal to tie it."

To Goings, the most egregious overtime coin flip decision this season was his favorite team's. Having either not read Goings' study or not agreed with his conclusions, New Orleans Saints coach Kellen Moore — after winning the toss — chose to kick the ball to Detroit in a 31-30 week 1 overtime loss to the Lions.

"They did the exact opposite of the strategy I suggested," Goings lamented. "That was pretty frustrating to watch."

articles.title: New Jaxson Dart Injury Update, Latest Giants Rumors Ahead of Knee Surgery
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is reportedly set to undergo knee surgery on Friday.
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is reportedly set to undergo knee surgery on Friday.

ESPN's Jordan Raanan reported the surgery is expected to address Dart's MCL and meniscus.

Dart will be out indefinitely, but head coach John Harbaugh left the door open for a potential postseason return should the Giants make it that far.

Top takeaways from Thursday Night Football

"I think I said it. I said it. Regular season," Harbaugh said of Dart's absence. "Other than that, how do you know? It depends on the recovery. You can't pinpoint it."

During the Giants' Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, Dart took a hard hit to his leg and was forced to exit the game. Though he reportedly lobbied to go back into the game, he did not return as New York lost 28-6.

Two days after the injury, it was reported that Dart suffered damage to his MCL, PCL and meniscus.

Dart threw for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions as a rookie, adding 487 rushing yards and nine scores on the ground.

Before Monday's injury, he started the season strong with a 230-yard, three-touchdown performance in a win over the Dallas Cowboys. That game gave Giants fans hope that the team was capable of a playoff run, but Dart's injury obviously threw a wrench in their plans.

While New York has a veteran backup in Jameis Winston, he struggled after coming in for Dart against the Rams, finishing 11-of-27 for 11 yards and an interception.

Winston is capable of big performances when he gets hot, but it's hard to say whether he's capable of leading a rebuilding Giants team to the playoffs.

articles.title: Tom Brady vs Patrick Mahomes - why TB12 Foundation could never match 15 and the Mahomies
articles.summary: Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady founded the TB12 Foundation in 2015. The operations closed in January 2026.
articles.body: Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady founded the TB12 Foundation in 2015. The operations closed in January 2026. The foundation was a nonprofit organization dedicated to maximizing the health, well-being, and athletic potential of underserved athletes and service members.The foundation provided free access to health and wellness resources that support preparation, performance, and recovery. It empowered people facing economic or health-related obstacles to reach their performance and life goals.Three-time Super Bowl champion Patrick Mahomes founded 15 and the Mahomies Foundation in 2019. The foundation is a nonprofit charity dedicated to improving children’s lives. The foundation supports initiatives that focus on health, wellness, communities in need of resources, and other charitable causes.The difference between Brady's and Mahomes's charitable foundations does not necessarily determine which did more meaningful work. Rather, their distinct missions, programs, fundraising models, and public initiatives have shaped their long-term visibility. For TB12, till January 2026.Tom Brady’s TB12 Foundation was focused on health and wellnessTom Brady’s TB12 Foundation’s programs included scholarships and partnerships designed to promote injury prevention, physical activity, and lifelong healthy habits.The foundation’s work was closely linked to the TB12 approach to health and athletic performance. That specific mission naturally gave the organization a narrower public footprint than a massive collection of highly visible youth initiatives.The foundation’s financial landscape shows a comparatively smaller operating footprint.According to ProPublica, the TB12 Foundation reported $13,529 in revenue and $224,913 in expenses for the fiscal year 2025.Its investment income accounted for most of its revenue [98.9%]. Net income was -$211,384 and net assets were $577,028. Of the notable expenses, executive compensation of $131,250 accounted for 58.4% of total expenses.Revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $7,000 higher than in 2025, at $20,220. Revenue was much higher in fiscal year 2023, at $289,546, with over $450,102 in expenses, -$160,556 net income, and over $1 million in net assets. Maybe the depreciating value made the NFL legend give up on it [just speculation here].15 and the Mahomies Foundation has broad youth focusThe 15 and the Mahomies Foundation has a broader youth-centered mission. Its programs include Read for 15, Volunteer for 15, 15 for 15, and college scholarships.The wide variety of programs creates more opportunities for children, families, schools, and volunteers to interact directly with the foundation.For instance, its Volunteer for 15 program mobilized nearly 2,000 youths who collectively dedicated over 80,000 service hours in 2024 to uplift communities across the U.S., Canada, and Uganda, creating more than $2.6 million in value for their communities. In 2025, that number increased 15% from 2024.In 2025, over 2000 youth volunteers across five countries [United States, Canada, Uganda, Nigeria, and Algeria] contributed over 92,000 hours of service and created more than $3.2 million in community impact.Financially, the foundation has a considerably large footprint. According to ProPublica’s Form 990, the foundation recorded $1.503 million in revenue and $1.518 million in expenses, with about 84% program efficiency for its fiscal year 2024. Its peak revenue came in 2021, at $1.83 million, while expenses stood at $1.98 million.Tom Brady vs Patrick Mahomes charity modelTB12 Foundation’s specialized health-and-performance mission closely aligned with Tom Brady’s broader wellness brand.Whereas Patrick Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies Foundation uses multiple, highly accessible youth programs and community partnerships.Mahomes’ foundation has also made numerous grants to outside organizations like Boys & Girls Clubs of America, Shelter KC, Youth Volunteer Corps, Pete’s Garden, Kansas City Pet Project, Special Olympics Missouri INC, and more, reporting 119 grants totaling $4.6 million between 2020 and 2024.TB12 Foundation made two grants to Tampa Bay Sports Commission INC totaling $50,000 between 2022 and 2023.The foundation received grants from four funders in fiscal year 2023: $145K from Givengain Foundation USA, $40K from National Football League Foundation, $9K from Bank of America Charitable Foundation INC, and $500 from Eastern Bank Charitable Foundation, totaling $195,000.Bottom line: available public data suggests that 15 and the Mahomies Foundation has a broader, more visible program structure. The TB12 Foundation operated on a comparatively smaller scale with a more specialized mission.This difference helps explain their distinctive public profiles without suggesting that popularity alone measures charitable impact. We all know Brady is more popular than Mahomes. But when it comes to TB12 vs. 15 and the Mahomies charity, Mahomes is likely the winner.PS: NFL legend Tom Brady announced via Instagram in January 2026 that TB12 was winding down.“TB12 Family, after an incredible run, TB12 is winding down. I’m grateful to everyone who believed in the mission. TB12 shaped how I see performance and wellness, and I’m proud of what we built together.Now, I’m excited to share the next chapter: NOBULL Nutrition. I want you to try something I believe in – no-bullsh*t products designed to help people get better mentally, emotionally, and physically. I can’t wait for us to build something new together. Mahomes wore the jersey during Kansas City’s 41-14 win on November 14, 2021, when he threw for 406 yards and five touchdowns. Against the Raiders, the Chiefs quarterback completed 35 of 50 passes for 406 yards and five touchdowns, finishing the game with a 127.6 passer rating.Kansas City controlled the game and secured a 41-14 road victory in Las Vegas. Mahomes was not sacked or hit during the contest, while his five touchdown passes helped the Chiefs put together a dominant performance.The jersey later ended up with DeSean Jackson, who was playing for the Raiders at the time. Mahomes signed the jersey and added a personal message for Jackson, giving the piece another connection to the game beyond Mahomes’ performance.The jersey was offered through Heritage Auctions as part of its Winter Sports Catalog Auction. The auction ran from December 5 through December 7, 2024, with the jersey selling for $192,000 on December 6 after attracting 18 registered phone and internet bidders.Why the 2021 game made Mahomes’ jersey specialThe jersey was more than a signed piece of Chiefs memorabilia because experts were able to connect it directly to Mahomes’ performance against the Raiders.Heritage Auctions said experts from Davious Sports photo-matched the jersey to images from the November 14 game. The identification included details such as the jersey’s mesh-hole pattern and loose threads that could be seen in photographs from the contest.The jersey also showed signs of actual game use, including sweat staining around the collar. However, it did not have turf or dirt marks, which fits with the fact that Mahomes was not sacked or hit during the game. This detail helps distinguish the jersey’s physical condition from memorabilia that shows visible contact with the field.The jersey featured Mahomes’ No. 15, his name on the back, and the AFC and Lamar Hunt patches. The interior collar also carried Nike and NFL on-field tags identifying it as a quarterback jersey.The auction lot included authentication documentation from Heritage Auctions, PSA/DNA, Beckett Authentication Services and Davious Sports.That kind of documentation can be important in the sports memorabilia market. A signed jersey can attract collectors, but a game-worn piece that can be linked to one specific performance gives buyers a much clearer connection to the player’s career.Mahomes has also seen other game-worn jerseys reach significant prices. A 2020 Chiefs jersey photo-matched to Kansas City’s November 22 game against the Raiders sold for $183,000 at Heritage Auctions in February 2025. Mahomes threw for 348 yards and two touchdowns in that 35-31 Chiefs victory.An earlier Mahomes jersey from his 2017 rookie season sold for $10,200 at Heritage Auctions in October 2018. That jersey was connected to a preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks and was described as game-worn, signed and unwashed.The $192,000 sale shows how collectors can place a higher value on memorabilia tied to a specific performance. Mahomes’ 2021 jersey combined a five-touchdown game, clear photo-matching evidence, physical signs of game use and a personal inscription to another NFL player, making it a distinctive piece from his Chiefs career.I also removed the earlier wording about “marks and darkened sweat staining” because it could imply contact with the turf. articles.title: Nick Bosa Injured, Latest Rumors on 49ers Star's Timeline to Return from Calf Issue
articles.summary: Even amid a strong 2-0 start to the season, the hits keep coming for the San Francisco 49ers with Nick Bosa set to miss time due to a calf injury.
articles.body:
Even amid a strong 2-0 start to the season, the hits keep coming for the San Francisco 49ers with Nick Bosa set to miss time due to a calf injury.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Bosa is expected to miss "a few weeks" after injuring his calf during Thursday's practice.

Not including Bosa's situation, the 49ers already lead the NFL with 15 players currently on injured reserve, as well as two players on the physically unable to perform list. The group includes five defensive linemen — Alfred Collins, CJ West, Sam Okuayinonu, Andrew Farmer and Mikail Kamara.

An IR stint for Bosa would keep him out for at least four weeks. If the 49ers were to make a move prior to Sunday's matchup with the Arizona Cardinals, the earliest he could return is Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons.

The 49ers' bye is in Week 8, which could factor into their strategy if it's determined Bosa needs to go injured reserve.

Mykel Williams, the No. 11 pick in the 2025 NFL draft, is on the physically unable to perform list as he continues to rehab from a torn ACL suffered in Week 9 last season.

There is good news for Williams after head coach Kyle Shanahan announced on Monday they will open his practice window next week and potentially putting him on track to play as soon as he is eligible in Week 5.

Even though Schefter noted Bosa was injured Thursday, he was officially listed as a DNP for the Niners' first practice of the week on Wednesday. He sat out their first practice going into Week 2 with a "Not injury related — resting; knee" designation.

There was some question about whether or not Bosa would be on the field for the start of the regular season as he was continuing to work his way back from a torn ACL. He didn't go through his first full practice until Sept. 2, eight days before their Week 1 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

Bosa played 36 of 61 defensive snaps against the Rams. He followed that up by being on the field for 40 of 59 defensive plays in Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins.

The 28-year-old recorded seven combined tackles, two tackles for loss and one quarterback hit through the first two games.

Keion White, Ogbo Okoronkwo and Khalid Kareem are currently the top four EDGE rushers on the Niners' active roster with Bosa injured.

After Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, San Francisco's next two games are at home against the Denver Broncos and on the road against the Seattle Seahawks.

articles.title: From a $1 million Detroit donation to a $1.5 million UGA gift: How Matthew and Kelly Stafford built a lasting charitable legacy
articles.summary: Matthew and Kelly Stafford have used their success in the NFL to support education, youth programs and community causes.
articles.body: Matthew and Kelly Stafford have used their success in the NFL to support education, youth programs and community causes. Much of their charitable work has a strong connection to Detroit, where Matthew played for the Lions for 12 seasons. Their giving has also reached the University of Georgia, where both have personal ties. Together, their documented donations include millions of dollars toward education, youth development and social justice programs.How Matthew and Kelly Stafford turned a $1 million gift into a lasting Detroit education centerThe Staffords’ relationship with SAY Detroit began in 2015, when the organization opened its Play Center in Detroit. The center provides free academic, athletic and arts programs, along with meals and transportation, for young people in the area. The Staffords became supporters of the center and later made one of their biggest commitments to the project.In February 2021, Matthew and Kelly Stafford pledged $1 million to help build a new education center at SAY Detroit Play Center at Lipke Park. The planned facility was named the Kelly and Matthew Stafford & Friends Education Center. The 15,000 square foot expansion was designed to add six classrooms, learning labs and a theater, while also creating space for vocational and technical training for adults.The project moved forward with support from other donors as well. SAY Detroit later reported that the Staffords, the A.A. Van Elslander Foundation and the Clarence and Jack Himmel Foundation each provided $1 million toward the expansion. More than 1,000 other donors also contributed to the project.The center was dedicated on April 1, 2024. SAY Detroit said the new space expanded the Play Center by nearly 15,000 square feet and allowed it to offer more academic and enrichment programs for hundreds of Detroit young people between the ages of 8 and 18. The facility also includes learning labs and a black box theater.Matthew and Kelly Stafford’s $1.5 million UGA donation supported social justice and scholarshipsTheir charitable work has also included the University of Georgia, where Matthew played football and Kelly was a cheerleader. In 2020, the couple committed $1.5 million to the university. The University of Georgia said the gift supported several areas, including a new social justice program within UGA Athletics.Of that commitment, $350,000 went toward the social justice program, which focused on diversity, inclusion, equity and social justice for student-athletes, coaches and staff. The gift also created two Georgia Commitment Scholarships for students who could still struggle to cover the full cost of attendance even after receiving other financial aid.The remaining parts of the $1.5 million commitment supported the Magill Society and the Butts-Mehre Expansion Project, as well as the UGA Spirit Program Operational Endowment, which provides support for Georgia cheerleading.The Staffords’ charitable work has therefore reached different parts of education, from a Detroit center serving children and adults to scholarships and student programs at their former university. articles.title: Cowboys' Jake Ferguson Fined by NFL For 'Imitation of Shotgunning a Beer' vs. Commanders
articles.summary: The NFL's crackdown on celebrations that are perceived to be pantomiming the consumption of alcohol continued Friday.
articles.body:
The NFL's crackdown on celebrations that are perceived to be pantomiming the consumption of alcohol continued Friday.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the NFL announced that it fined Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson $13,611 for his "imitation of shotgunning a beer" after scoring a touchdown in the team's 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 2:

The league noted that the celebration "constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably could be construed as being in poor taste."

Ferguson's fine comes after the NFL fined San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk $14,926 on Thursday for an "imitation of chugging a beer" during the Niners' 35-13 Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins.

Juszczyk, whose nickname is "Juice," pushed back against the NFL's assertion on Thursday, telling reporters that he was mimicking drinking juice rather than a beer.

The veteran fullback subsequently appealed the fine and will have a hearing on Tuesday, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner .

It is unclear if Ferguson will appeal as well, although it may be tougher for him to make a case that his "shotgunning" celebration wasn't meant to reference beer.

Ferguson, 27, is a two-time Pro Bowler who bounced back from a slow start to his 2026 season after recording just two catches for six yards in a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants in Week 1.

In Dallas' convincing victory over Washington, Ferguson finished with four receptions for 43 yards and a pair of touchdowns from quarterback Dak Prescott.

Ferguson set career highs with 82 receptions and eight touchdowns last season, and he continues to be a key part of the Cowboys' high-powered offense along with Prescott, wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, and running back Javonte Williams.

Dallas will look to improve to 2-1 on the season Sunday when it hosts the 1-1 Baltimore Ravens.

articles.title: Drew and Brittany Brees’ Brees Dream Foundation has contributed over $50 million to support cancer patients and children

articles.body: Drew Brees was officially inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame as part of the Class of 2026. He was inducted alongside Larry Fitzgerald, Luke Kuechly, Adam Vinatieri, and Roger Craig.Brees entered the league in 2001 and announced his retirement in March 2021. He played elite-level quarterback in 20 NFL seasons, with a Super Bowl win and 13 Pro Bowl selections.As much as he cherished the gridiron, he gave twice the effort off it. Since 2003, the New Orleans Saints legend and his wife, Brittany Brees, have used the Brees Dream Foundation to support cancer patients, children, and families in need.According to its official website, the foundation has contributed more than $50 million to charitable causes globally since its inception.Drew and Brittany Brees’ Brees Dream Foundation and cancer supportDrew and Brittany Brees’ Brees Dream Foundation’s mission is “improving the quality of life for cancer patients, and providng care, education, and opportunities for children and families in need.”In 2010, Drew Brees secured a $100,000 grant for New Orleans’ Patrick F. Taylor Hope Lodge, a place for out-of-town cancer patients and caregivers to stay for free while they undergo treatment.The New Orleans Hope Lodge used the grant to help fund ongoing services to patients and caregivers, including apartment-style housing complete with community-hosted dinners, laundry, library, and free transportation to local cancer centers.Drew Brees also supports cancer research with his Brees Dream Foundation. The organization works toward advancing cancer research and providing care, education, and opportunities for at-need children.Drew Brees’ foundation teams up with Ochsner HealthIn 2020, the Drew Brees’ foundation joined with Ochsner Health to improve access to services such as prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and management of diseases, illnesses, disorders, and other health-impacting conditions.The foundation invested in three community health centers across Louisiana: New Orleans East, Baton Rouge, and Gretna.Since 2023, the centers have cared for nearly 60,000 patients by providing accessible, convenient healthcare services to community residents. The centers provide primary and pediatric care, along with screenings and health education.Drew Brees Foundation’s support for childrenChildren and education are the Brees Dream Foundation’s second major focus, after cancer. Its mission particularly covers providing care, education, and opportunities for children and families in need. Its grants have supported organizations working to provide young people with educational and economic opportunities.For instance, the foundation has partnered with Junior Achievement of Greater New Orleans for the Trust Your Crazy Ideas Challenge program.It gives high school students across the region a chance to develop their own startup idea and pitch it for $15,000 in scholarship money and a year of free Chick-fil-A.In March 2026, Alvin, Brianna, and Marianne of Biofresh Containers won $5,000 in scholarship money and a year of free Chick-fil-A.Since 2014, nearly 20,000 students from Shreveport, Monroe, Baton Rouge, Lafayette, Greater New Orleans, the North Shore, and the Mississippi Gulf Coast have answered the Trust Your Crazy Ideas Challenge.The program has provided over 410,000 in scholarships and over $130,000 in funds to schools to support entrepreneurial education.Young entrepreneurs are solving today’s issues with tomorrow’s innovations: from language learning apps to emergency power stations.“Who knows? Some of the ideas that these students develop could be the ideas that push New Orleans forward,” Drew Brees said.Junior Achievement of Greater New Orleans’ programs help young people develop knowledge and skills in financial literacy, career preparation, and economic decision-making. These skills help children make smarter academic and financial decisions.Brees Dream Foundation’s BuildStrong AcademyIn April 2022, Drew Brees brought BuildStrong Academy to New Orleans. The Super Bowl champion’s The Brees Dream Foundation sponsors it.Brees shared the excitement via Instagram post, “Proud and honored to bring BuildStrong Academy to New Orleans!!One of the very first chapters in the country, providing free training, certification and placement in the skilled construction trades! A life changer for a lot of people! articles.title: Why Tom Brady felt ‘embarrassed’ after swearing on FOX as NFL legend addresses unexpected broadcast mishap
articles.summary: Tom Brady has admitted he was “kind of embarrassed” after using profanity during FOX’s broadcast of the Dallas Cowboys’ 37-20 win over the Washington
articles.body: Tom Brady has admitted he was “kind of embarrassed” after using profanity during FOX’s broadcast of the Dallas Cowboys’ 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders. The former quarterback’s comment came during a big play from Dak Prescott, when Brady described the Cowboys quarterback’s deep throw to CeeDee Lamb in unusually blunt terms. The remark quickly spread online, adding to another uncomfortable moment from the same broadcast when Brady also reacted to Jayden Daniels’ serious elbow injury with an expletive. Days later, Brady addressed his language and said he plans to clean it up on future FOX broadcasts.Why did Tom Brady apologize for his FOX broadcast comments?Tom Brady’s first slip came during Prescott’s 35-yard completion to Lamb in the fourth quarter. The throw drew an excited response from the seven-time Super Bowl champion, who called it an “absolute piss missile up the sideline.”The phrase quickly became one of the most talked-about parts of the broadcast. Brady later acknowledged that the wording was not ideal for a network NFL telecast, particularly one watched by families.“I’m actually kind of embarrassed,” Brady said. “There’s a lot of grandmas at home that probably aren’t very happy with my mouth on FOX. I’m going to fix that. Sorry, I apologize.”Brady also joked that his family has noticed his recent run of colorful language. He said, “That swear jar is getting way too full in my house,” before adding, “My kids are getting way too happy with me filling up that jar.”That detail gave the incident a lighter edge, but Brady’s comments also showed that he understands the difference between talking football among players and doing it on a major television broadcast.What else did Tom Brady say during the Cowboys-Commanders game?The Prescott comment was not Tom Brady’s only verbal mishap that afternoon.Earlier in the game, Daniels suffered a dislocated left elbow after landing awkwardly. As FOX showed a replay of the injury, Brady reacted instinctively with an expletive before quickly apologizing and acknowledging that he had not expected to see such a graphic moment on the broadcast.The two incidents came during a broadcast that otherwise gave Brady plenty to discuss. Prescott threw for 207 yards and three touchdowns in Dallas’ victory, while Daniels left the game and was replaced by Marcus Mariota.For Brady, though, the attention afterward shifted away from his football analysis and toward his choice of words.That is part of the adjustment that comes with moving from the quarterback position to the broadcast booth. On the field, Brady spent decades reacting in the moment. On television, those reactions reach millions of viewers instantly.His latest comments suggest he knows he has to make that adjustment. articles.title: 49ers' Nick Bosa reportedly expected to miss 'a few weeks' after pulling calf during practice
articles.summary: The five-time Pro Bowl defensive end suffered the setback during Thursday's practice, according to multiple reports.
articles.body:
Injuries have been a thorn in Nick Bosa 's side, and the latest is reportedly expected to sideline him for "a few weeks."

The five-time Pro Bowl defensive end pulled his calf during Thursday's practice and is now out, including for Sunday's Week 3 game against the Arizona Cardinals , ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Friday.

San Francisco is reportedly weighing whether Bosa needs to be placed on injured reserve. If he goes on IR, he'll have to miss a minimum of four games.

Bosa, 28, played in only three games last season. He tore his right ACL in Week 3 of the 2025 campaign versus the Cardinals. That marked the third ACL tear of his football career.

He also suffered a left ACL tear in 2020, in Week 2 of his second season in the league.

With two season-ending injuries already disrupting his NFL career, it was up in the air if Bosa would return in time for this season's opener, what turned out to be the Niners' 27-7 beatdown of the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia . The former NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year (2019) and Defensive Player of the Year (2022) suited up Down Under and turned in four total tackles, registering a pair of tackles for a loss in the process. By the time San Francisco's 35-13 victory over the Miami Dolphins wrapped in Week 2, he was tied for the team lead with six pressures, according to Next Gen Stats.

It wasn't unusual for Bosa to sit out Wednesday's practice, the team's first practice of the week, given his veteran status and injury history. At the time, he was listed as a nonparticipant, with the designation of "resting player/knee." But on Thursday, a day on which the Niners added "calf" next to his name on the team's injury report, he reportedly joined the 49ers ' battalion of injured personnel.

Although San Francisco is 2-0, it is once again dealing with a rash of recovering players. The 49ers' defensive line is navigating several absences. Defensive tackle C.J. West landed on IR with a knee issue this week. During the first two weeks of the season, defensive end Sam Okuayinonu and defensive tackle Alfred Collins were lost to IR, too, because of foot and patellar tendon injuries, respectively, that they picked up in practice.

Plus, a high ankle sprain is keeping defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. out three-to-six weeks. And there's no guarantee edge rusher Romello Height plays Sunday against the Cardinals, as he's weathering a broken hand and hasn't practiced so far this week .

That list doesn't even include defensive end Mykel Williams , whom the 49ers selected 11th overall in last year's draft. Like Bosa, a torn ACL threw a wrench in his 2025 season. He's still on the physically unable-to-perform list and isn't eligible to return to game action until San Francisco's Week 5 matchup versus the Seattle Seahawks .

Additionally, the 49ers are juggling a batch of wide receiver injuries .

articles.title: Bijan Robinson Clarifies Viral Remarks About Kevin Stefanski's Falcons Locker Room Speech

articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons star running back Bijan Robinson provided some clarification after comparing head coach Kevin Stefanski's locker room speech to civil rights activist Martin Luther King Jr. following the team's 0-2 start.

"Yup I just saying stuff sometimes lol. Was a awesome speech for the team though," Robinson wrote in a Friday post on X.

The Falcons fell to the Pittsburgh Steelers and Carolina Panthers in their first two games of the 2026 season, but bounced back with a 35-14 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night.

Stefanski joked about Robinson's comparison following the win against Green Bay.

"I don't think Dr. King used as many f-bombs as I did," Stefanski said Friday, per ESPN's Marc Raimondi .

He's in the midst of his first year patrolling the sidelines for the Falcons after he was hired as their head coach on Jan. 17.

Despite the slow start to the season, Atlanta's offense put together a dominant performance on Thursday night.

The Falcons finished with 498 total yards, as they didn't punt during the second half of the contest.

Robinson was a key part of Atlanta's success, as the two-time Pro Bowler finished with 194 rush yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries. He also caught two passes for 19 yards.

The 24-year-old has already amassed 349 yards on the ground through three appearances in 2026 after racking up 2,298 all-purpose yards and 11 total touchdowns during his 2025 campaign.

It's worth noting that Thursday marked the season debut of quarterback Michael Penix Jr., who played in his first game since Nov. 2025 after recovering from a torn ACL .

Backup passer Cooper Rush started for Atlanta during the first two weeks of the year.

Now, the Falcons will look to continue building momentum during a Week 4 clash with the New Orleans Saints.

articles.title: Packers tight end Tucker Kraft hears boos from Lambeau Field fans and offers tone deaf response
articles.summary: Tucker Kraft called Lambeau Field booing "pretty disappointing" after the Green Bay Packers' blowout home loss to the Atlanta Falcons Thursday.
articles.body: Green Bay Packers tight end Tucker Kraft dropped a couple of passes during Thursday night's blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons, which was indicative of his team's stunningly inept performance that caused the Lambeau Field crowd to boo the home team. And Kraft was stunned by that. Hurt by that. No, not the loss. The booing. BROWNS PICK DESHAUN WATSON AS THEIR STARTING QB DESPITE HOME CROWD BOOING AND HIS '17 AWAY GAMES' COMMENT "Yeah, it’s pretty tough," Kraft told reporters huddled around his locker stall. "You know, like everyone pictures Lambeau Field and not boos. I don't picture boos. I picture my home stadium. That's tough. It's pretty disappointing." Friends, it is 2026 not 1966. So, the Packers of Vince Lombardi, Ray Nitschke, Jim Taylor, Herb Adderly, Willie Wood, Jerry Kramer and the other men who made this franchise a beacon of excellence and toughness and turned Green Bay into Titletown are a long-ago memory. Now, we've got these Packers, who lost their last five games last season, and collapsed in giving up a big lead to lose their season-opener this season, and then lost their home-opener against the Falcons on Thursday night. And these guys are complaining about being booed. FROM THE CHARGERS TO THE COLTS AND FALCONS, WHICH OF THE NFL'S EIGHT WINLESS TEAMS ARE ALREADY IN PANIC MODE These Packers got run out of Lambeau Field by a previously winless team. So, darn right, the fans booed. But Kraft, who heard the boos, is tone-deaf. "It's pretty disappointing," Kraft continued. "It's not gonna help us win. Like, I don't know, I don't know what people think that's gonna rally us or something like that. "But, you know, we're grown men. We're mentally strong enough, capable enough to get back on the field and play ball. Um, but, probably much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us." This is not the way, Tucker Kraft. You just signed a $75 million contract extension. You got $26.5 million of that in a signing bonus. So, just for signing your name on the document, you collected more money than most of your fans make in their lifetimes by a multiple of 10. And you don't understand why they're unhappy when you and your teammates do not perform? You don't picture boos? Fans didn't picture their team giving up 27 unanswered points to the Falcons. Fans didn't picture their team rushing for a grand total of 17 yards. Or the defense giving up 242 rushing yards. And nobody pictured Kraft suddenly talking about them, as if Deshaun Watson suddenly took over his body. The stunning part is that Kraft is one of the most stand-up guys on the Packers. He is a tough player. He fights back from injuries. He is not a victim. But this was full-on soft victim mentality. To be fair: This is not all Kraft talked about after the game. He talked about rallying and even admitted to not playing "to my standard." But that's the minimum-expected reaction after what fans have witnessed going back to December 2025. What no one expects is a team leader in any way lecturing fans that showed their displeasure the only way they really can. Those people pay to be in the stadium and have the right to express their displeasure in this manner. Some fans at other venues throw beer bottles. Kraft, his teammates and coaches have been giving the fans plenty to be displeased about. And the only proper response to the question about being booed on Thursday night was, "We deserved it and will try to do better." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.summary: Former NFL running back, four-time Pro Bowler and Cleveland Browns legend Nick Chubb signed a one-day contract with his old team to officially retire as a Brown on Friday.
articles.body:
Former NFL running back, four-time Pro Bowler and Cleveland Browns legend Nick Chubb signed a one-day contract with his old team to officially retire as a Brown on Friday.

Speaking to reporters at his press conference, Chubb was reflective when recounting his journey with the Browns, which included a severe knee injury in 2023.

The Browns will honor Chubb on Sunday, when the team will host its 2026 home opener against the Carolina Panthers.

The Browns selected Chubb, a former Georgia star, with the 35th overall pick in the 2018 NFL draft.

Chubb had authored an amazing comeback story in college after suffering a devastating left knee injury (dislocated kneecap, torn PCL, MCL and LCL) in 2015 . He rebounded with 2,591 yards from scrimmage and 24 touchdowns over the 2016 and 2017 seasons.

In the pros, Chubb immediately became the Browns' top running back and offensive weapon. He helped quickly turn around a team that went 0-16 the year before his arrival. Cleveland improved to 7-8-1 in Chubb's rookie season (2018) and made the playoffs for the first time in 18 years in 2020 after an 11-5 season.

The Browns also won their first playoff game since 1994, beating the AFC North champion Pittsburgh Steelers in the AFC Wild Card round.

Over his first five seasons, Chubb amassed 7,331 yards from scrimmage and 52 touchdowns. He had four 1,000-yard rushing seasons (2019-2022) and even made the All-Pro Second Team in 2022.

Chubb got off to a hot start in 2023, rushing for 170 yards on just 28 carries. Sadly, Chubb suffered a torn MCL and a damaged ACL in his left knee in Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Chubb missed the rest of the 2023 season and the first six games of 2024. Unfortunately, Chubb's remarkably efficient form from his first six seasons (5.3 yards per carry) did not appear post-injury. He played one more season with Cleveland (2024) and a final campaign with the Houston Texans (2025). Thankfully, Chubb suited up for a near-full season in 2025 (15 games), amassing 573 yards and three scores.

For his career, Chubb finished with 8,458 yards from scrimmage and 59 touchdowns on 1,603 touches (5.3 yards per touch). He averaged 5.0 yards per carry.

There's no doubt Chubb was one of the NFL's best running backs of the past 10 years. Despite playing only five full seasons as an RB1, Chubb is ninth in the NFL in rushing yards since 2016.

Now he'll get his well-deserved love and respect from Cleveland faithful this week as Chubb officially retires as a Brown.

articles.body: ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith has put the focus on one issue before Texas faces Tennessee: Arch Manning cannot afford to waste his chances.
