articles.title: NFLPA President Says Brazil Field for Cowboys vs. Ravens Was Upgraded for Better Stability, Traction
articles.summary: NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter revealed that the field at Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, the site of a Week 3 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens, has been upgraded.
articles.body:
NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter revealed that the field at Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, the site of a Week 3 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens, has been upgraded.

"We've been in regular communication with the league about the field," Tretter wrote as part of a post on X. "Both the NFLPA's and the league's field experts have been on the ground in Brazil for days, monitoring conditions and working to make the surface as safe and playable as possible for Sunday. Based on our experts' assessment, the field needed better traction and stability. They recommended reinforced stitching to help the surface hold together and brought in equipment to reinforce as much of the field as possible before the game. Our experts will remain engaged and continue evaluating conditions through kickoff."

Soccer players previously complained about the field quality ahead of the game.

"You don't even need to talk about the field. It's there for everyone to see," Flamengo goalkeeper Agustín Rossi said, according to ge, a Brazilian sports media site (h/t Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner) . "The way we play, it's unbelievable that we're playing on a field like this. Both penalty areas are bad as [expletive]. If you look at it, there are bumps everywhere. There's still going to be an NFL game here during the international break. After that game, I hope the field is in better shape."

On Monday, NFL field director Nick Pappas told Jon Machota, Jeff Zrebiec and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic that there were "no concerns" about the playing surface.

The venue utilized a GrassMaster Stitch Machine to directly stitch synthetic polypropylene fibers into the natural grass field in order to increase resistance on Thursday (h/t Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk).

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson wasn't too worried about the field conditions.

"I believe the NFL does a great job at having their specialists go out there and look over the fields," Jackson said Wednesday, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley . "I cannot worry about that. I just have to worry about getting us a dub in Brazil. [As for] the field, we have played on bad fields plenty of times, so I cannot really dwell on that."

The upcoming clash will mark the third NFL regular-season game to take place in Brazil. The first two contests occurred in São Paulo.

Both the Cowboys and Ravens sit at 1-1 this year as they look to contend in their respective divisions.

Baltimore is coming off a 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 2, while Dallas wrapped up a 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders.

Kickoff between the Cowboys and Ravens is on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Doubftul for Rams vs. Broncos With Injury, Top Waiver-Wire WR Replacements for Fantasy
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is doubtful to play against the Denver Broncos, Sean McVay told reporters Friday, although the head coach did provide some good news:
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is doubtful to play against the Denver Broncos, Sean McVay told reporters Friday, although the head coach did provide some good news:

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport previously reported Nacua was "unlikely to play" on Sunday evening as he continues to deal with hip and groin concerns:

As noted by ESPN's Sarah Barshop , Nacua is listed with a hip ailment on the Rams' injury report. McVay told reporters the wideout is also dealing with "a little bit of soreness" in his groin. He missed his second straight practice on Thursday.

So it appears Nacua will now miss his second straight game after sitting the Rams' 28-6 home win over the New York Giants in Week 2.

From a fantasy perspective, here's a look at five wide receivers to consider if players need a starter in Nacua's place. All players listed here are available in 51 percent or more in Yahoo leagues.

Baltimore Ravens WR Rashod Bateman (Available in 68% of Leagues)

Miami Dolphins WR Malik Washington (84%)

With Zay Flowers ( hamstring ) sidelined last week, Baltimore Ravens wideout Rashod Bateman caught seven passes for 88 yards and a touchdown on nine targets in a 24-17 home loss to the New Orleans Saints.

Flowers hasn't practiced this week, putting his availability in doubt for the Ravens' matchup with the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil on Sunday.

Only two players had more than three targets last Sunday: Bateman and tight end Mark Andrews (seven). The guess here is quarterback Lamar Jackson looks Bateman's way frequently again.

Like the Ravens, the Houston Texans lost their No. 1 wide receiver (Nico Collins) to a hamstring injury in Week 2. Collins hasn't practiced in Week 3, leaving his status in doubt for Sunday at the Indianapolis Colts.

Texans' playmakers had chances to step up last Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals, but the offense struggled in a 20-6 defeat.

This Sunday brings more chances for success against a Colts team that's allowed 74 points in two weeks. That means wide receiver Keyshon Boutte could get his time to shine. Boutte had a quiet game Sunday (three catches, 37 yards), but he played a healthy 72 percent of the snaps and could certainly break out here.

This is a spot where it's hard to ignore the production. Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Tre Tucker broke out for 119 yards and a touchdown on five catches (seven targets) in a 26-14 road win over the Los Angeles Chargers last Sunday. Clearly, he has found a good rapport with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins.

Granted, the Raiders' top pass-catcher (tight end Brock Bowers) was out with a knee ailment. He may be back Sunday at the New Orleans Saints after logging a pair of practices this week.

Still, Tucker is clearly the Raiders' top wideout right now, so he'll get his looks. And the Raiders' offense did well thanks in large part to his efforts, so one can surmise the team should go back to that well Sunday.

The Miami Dolphins are banged up at wideout heading into a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. Caleb Douglas has missed both practices this week, and Chris Bell suited up for both, albeit in limited fashion.

This may be a spot for Malik Washington to rise. Washington leads the team in targets with 13 through two weeks, though it hasn't translated into much production (seven catches, 96 yards). Still, Washington will have opportunities, maybe even more now that Douglas is potentially out.

Chicago Bears wide receiver Kalif Raymond leads the team in receptions (13), receiving yards (124) and targets (14), and that would have been near-impossible to predict before the season given a roster including tight end Colston Loveland and wideouts Rome Odunze and Luther Burden. Alas, he's the top producer right now.

It's unclear how long that will last, but it's at least worth considering riding the lightning right now and hoping Raymond stays hot.

There is a big question at quarterback, of course, with starter Caleb Williams (hamstring) and backup Tyson Bagent (concussion protocol) not practicing this week , leaving third-stringer (but capable veteran) Case Keenum as the possible starter. However, Raymond is getting his fair share of opportunities, and that could very well continue Monday.

articles.title: Rams' Puka Nacua doubtful for Broncos game, expected to return in Week 4
articles.summary: Nacua missed the Rams' Week 2 win over the Giants with groin soreness.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are likely to be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for a second straight week as he will be doubtful for Sunday night's matchup with the Denver Broncos .

Head coach Sean McVay told ESPN Los Angeles earlier this week that Nacua was "not making great progress" in his recovery from groin soreness that kept him out of the Rams' Monday night win over the New York Giants .

The injury is not a long-term concern, McVay added, and the team is just being cautious.

"When you're a skill player and you're really trying to hit high-speed yards and really open up and you feel just ... it's like some of the things that can almost be like pre-hernia is kind of what he's feeling," McVay said . "And so you err on the side of caution. Usually time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal. And then once you get to a certain point, then I think you feel pretty good moving forward."

On Friday, McVay said that barring a setback they expect Nacua to be available for Week 4 when they play the Philadelphia Eagles .

What Nacua is dealing with now is not related to the psoas issue that caused him to miss time during training camp. He was healthy enough to play Week 1 during the Rams' loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Nacua caught five passes on nine targets for 74 yards.

Nacua has not practiced this week and McVay said that the team is not considering placing him on injured reserve.

"We all want him to be able to be out there, but we want him to be able to return to performance, not just be able to just kind of gut through it," McVay said.

articles.title: Making sense of yet another 49ers rash of injuries, with Nick Bosa the latest victim
articles.summary: The 49ers' bad injury luck has been going on for most of Kyle Shanahan's time in San Fran, but also before that.
articles.body:
The 49ers ' Week 1 victory over the Rams was a demonstration of just how potent a healthy version of their team can be. Everything since has been a painful reminder that they apparently can't have nice things before they break.

The latest bad injury news arrived Friday with Nick Bosa 's calf, which apparently will keep him out multiple weeks . The star pass rusher suffered a torn ACL a year ago and was limited to three games in 2025. In the first two games of the season, he'd been limited to 60 total snaps.

This has left their defensive line in bad shape beyond Bosa. Alfred Collins is out for the season. Mykel Williams is on the PUP list and can't play until at least Week 5. C.J. West and Sam Okuayinonu currently reside on injured reserve. Oh, and don't forget James Thompson Jr., who's out multiple weeks, and rookie Romello Height, who just had hand surgery.

Wide receiver also has been decimated. Ricky Pearsall , De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk are all on IR as well. The team is also navigating injuries to Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle).

There are other notable injuries elsewhere, with TE Jake Tonges , LB Nick Martin and OT Austen Pleasants all on IR as well. On and on it goes.

And get this: ESPN's Adam Schefter just floated the idea that the Niners might not place Bosa on IR because they're worried about running out of return designations — each team only gets eight for the regular season.

Yeah, that's how bad things are. And it's Week 3.

The 49ers are 2-0, with three of the next four games at home. Then they'll play on the road at Seattle and at Atlanta in Weeks 5 and 7, respectively, prior to the Week 8 bye. Most teams like a well-placed bye, and many playoff contenders wouldn't mind one on the back half of the schedule as a way of resting players for the postseason grind.

But the 49ers might have preferred an even earlier bye, given that their health crisis has once again reared its ugly head.

What to make of another ridiculous rash of 49ers ailments

The Niners' annual injury woes are not a new story . It has even set off one of the wilder conspiracy theories in the NFL: that a nearby power substation is to blame. The fact that the substation was expanded in 2014 — right about when the Niners' annual injury overload began — and that so many of their injuries have occurred in practice, has only fueled the hilariously sad conspiracy madness.

Beyond the gallows humor, there's a bigger question: Why? And can you give a response that doesn't include "substation" in the answer?

Kyle Shanahan has typically favored a veteran roster, and this year's Opening Day group was the league's oldest at 27.49 years. It also featured a league-high 14 players over the age of 30. Older players tend to get hurt more often than younger ones.

That might explain some of the issues they've faced, but the 49ers haven't always had the league's oldest roster before. When Shanahan took over in 2017, they were one of the younger teams, and the older-roster trend has really only kicked up over the past five seasons or so.

But the one season, in 2023, they went relatively unscathed — at least compared to the carnage they've suffered for the remainder of the decade — they went to the Super Bowl. Dumb luck or some deeper pattern? It's very hard to say.

Shanahan also has been known as a coach who favors faster and more intense practices , perhaps more so than other teams do. Players who have played for Shanahan and other head coaches have pointed out that discrepancy . That might have something to do with the matter.

Shanahan's Thursday padded practices also appear to be more intense than how other teams typically handle those sessions. Bosa is a good example of this, but most of the remainder of the 49ers' injuries this season did not happen on Thursdays, so that theory might not be complete.

Others have speculated that because the 49ers practice and play on natural grass, they're more prone to injuries on turf fields. That theory caught some fire after the 49ers' bloodbath at MetLife Stadium in New York after a rash of injuries they suffered there (including Bosa) in the 2020 season, playing there two straight games. The theory was even revived when Williams suffered his torn ACL there.

But the problem is, the current 49ers haven't played at MetLife this season and their first two games were on natural grass. Some of the injuries have happened on grass at their Santa Clara practice fields. So that can't explain it fully either.

It might just be a fluky set of circumstances, or perhaps there are multiple factors — including some mentioned above — that have crippled this team more than others.

articles.title: Nick Bosa is ruled out again as his comeback lasts just two games, Cardinals curse continues
articles.summary: Nick Bosa's long-awaited return to the San Francisco 49ers has hit another frustrating roadblock.
articles.body: Nick Bosa's long-awaited return to the San Francisco 49ers has hit another frustrating roadblock. The star defensive end suffered a calf injury during Thursday's practice and is expected to miss a few weeks, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. Bosa will miss Sunday's Week 3 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, with the 49ers still determining whether he will be placed on injured reserve. The latest setback comes just two games into Bosa's return from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season after only three appearances.Nick Bosa had only just made his returnBosa entered the 2026 season after spending much of the previous year working his way back from the second ACL injury of his NFL career. The 49ers had been cautious with his workload throughout the offseason. San Francisco general manager John Lynch said before training camp that Bosa had been cleared to begin working his way back, while emphasizing that the team would gradually increase his workload during his recovery.That patience appeared to pay off when Bosa was available for the season opener against the Los Angeles Rams. He then played again in Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins. According to the 49ers' official player log, Bosa recorded four tackles and three tackles for loss in Week 1 before adding three tackles against Miami in Week 2.Now, instead of building momentum after his comeback, Bosa is facing another spell on the sidelines. The calf issue surfaced only days before the 49ers were scheduled to face the Cardinals, the same team Bosa was playing against when he suffered his ACL injury last season.Bosa was initially listed as dealing with soreness during training camp and had been managed carefully as he returned from the ACL injury. This time, however, the injury is expected to keep him out for multiple weeks.The 49ers are reportedly considering injured reserve, although the team is leaning against that option at this stage. If Bosa is placed on IR, he would be required to miss at least four games.49ers' defensive line takes another hitBosa's absence is also significant because San Francisco is already dealing with injuries along its defensive front. The team has had several defensive linemen miss time, adding pressure on the remaining players to fill Bosa's role while he recovers. The 49ers' official injury report has also listed defensive linemen including Romello Height and James Thompson Jr. among players missing practice this week.For a defense built around Bosa's ability to generate pressure off the edge, replacing his production will be a major challenge. The five-time Pro Bowler remains one of the centerpiece players on San Francisco's defense, making even a short-term absence particularly significant.Bosa now faces another recovery processThere is no indication at this point that the calf injury is connected to another ACL problem, and the current reporting points to an absence of a few weeks, rather than a season-ending injury.That distinction is important given what Bosa has already gone through. He missed almost the entirety of the 2025 season after tearing his ACL in Week 3 and spent the offseason working toward his return. articles.title: Pete Golding sends blunt Lane Kiffin message after Ole Miss victory as LSU loss adds tension to SEC rivalry
articles.summary: Pete Golding did not call Ole Miss’ 32-24 win over LSU a Super Bowl, but he admitted beating Lane Kiffin carried extra feeling after the game.
articles.body: Pete Golding did not call Ole Miss’ 32-24 win over LSU a Super Bowl, but he admitted beating Lane Kiffin carried extra feeling after the game. Speaking on The Rich Eisen Show, Golding said he would try to beat Kiffin whether they were playing football or pickleball. The comment added a personal edge to Kiffin’s return to Oxford, even as Golding stressed that the Rebels have bigger goals this season.Pete Golding admits Lane Kiffin matchup meant something to Ole Miss“Whether I’m playing Kiffin in pickleball or football, I’m trying to whoop his a**,” Golding said on The Rich Eisen Show. “So there was that piece of it. After it, I was excited for our players and our administration, you know, and our staff who put a lot into it.”Golding had been careful after the game to keep the focus away from Kiffin. He said the victory was important, but it was not the reason Ole Miss worked through the offseason. That view has not changed. The Rebels are 3-0 and have already moved on to another ranked SEC game at Florida.Golding worked with Kiffin at Alabama before becoming Ole Miss’ head coach after Kiffin left for LSU. Their teams met in Oxford with both ranked inside the top 10.“I think beating any good team and any good football coach, and I put Kiffin in that category, you know, and it was no different than playing Kirby in the Sugar Bowl,” Golding said. “I mean, when you play good teams that are coached really well, like you got to get them prepared and you got to make good decisions, but your players got to go out there and execute at a high level.”Lane Kiffin and Pete Golding leave Ole Miss with bigger goals aheadOle Miss built a 24-7 halftime lead before LSU fought back and tied the score. Trinidad Chambliss then answered with a 14-yard touchdown run, and Jaylon Braxton ended LSU’s final threat with an interception in the end zone.Chambliss completed 33 of 48 passes for 363 yards and two touchdowns, according to the Associated Press. articles.title: With Penix back at quarterback, Falcons show resiliency in win that restores hope for the season
articles.summary: Just four days after their most lopsided home loss ever at Mercedes-Benz Stadium — which had fans booing in the first quarter — the Atlanta Falcons pulled of...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Just four days after their most lopsided home loss ever at Mercedes-Benz Stadium — which had fans booing in the first quarter — the Atlanta Falcons pulled off an overwhelming bounce-back win that restored hope for the season.

This time, it was the Green Bay Packers who heard boos from their fans. Quarterback Michael Penix Jr., who played in his first game in 10 months, was a difference-maker for the Falcons (1-2) in their surprising 35-14 win at Green Bay on Thursday night.

Penix completed 18 of 25 passes for 256 yards with one touchdown and one interception. After throwing an interception on the Falcons' first drive, Penix went on to complete 16 of 18 passes in the final three quarters.

For perhaps the final time this season, coach Kevin Stefanski was asked Friday if Penix would remain the starter in the Falcons' next game. "Confirmed," Stefanski said.

"I'm proud of how Mike played. I know he can build upon that. I know he wants to be better."

Indeed, the much-anticipated quarterback competition between Penix and Tua Tagovailoa was never a race. Penix's recovery after tearing the ACL in his left knee during a loss to Carolina on Nov. 16 and Tagovailoa's oblique injury left both inactive for the first two weeks.

With Cooper Rush the starting quarterback, the Falcons scored a combined 16 points in their first two games, including an embarrassing 34-3 home loss to Carolina on Sunday. With Penix behind center, the Falcons scored 27 unanswered points. Bijan Robinson rushed for 194 yards and Drake London added 194 receiving yards.

Atlanta's balanced offense produced 498 yards — 242 rushing and 256 passing.

Safety Jessie Bates III said he "absolutely" expected the Falcons to play like winners.

"We knew what this team was about," Bates said. "Those first two weeks was not who we were at all. I think, obviously, with Mike Penix coming back that brought us some juice. As a team, when you can stop the run and run the ball at that level that we did today, you're going to win a lot of ball games like that."

The Falcons played winning football on offense, defense and special teams.

Penix answered the quarterback question but Stefanski stressed the win was not about one player. The Falcons outrushed the Packers 242-17 — the fewest rushing yards allowed in team history. Atlanta's pass rush put constant pressure on Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love .

Zach Harrison 's blocked field goal attempt was a highlight for the special teams.

While tight end Austin Hooper had a touchdown catch, Kyle Pitts had only one catch for five yards. Stefanski insisted again on Friday Pitts' lack of targets in the first three games is not an indication of what he expects to come.

"When a defense plays a certain way the ball goes where it goes," Stefansk said. "Kyle is going to be a big part of this offense. ... Kyle will be a huge part of what we do."

Penix's return had a dramatic impact on London's production. London had nine receptions for a career-high 194 yards. His 10 targets matched his combined total for the first two games.

Rush was inactive as the emergency third quarterback. Tagovailoa, who had been inactive the first two weeks while recovering from an oblique injury, was Penix's backup. If the Falcons view undrafted rookie Jack Strand as a player with developmental value, Rush's roster spot could be at risk if a need develops at another position and keeping four quarterbacks is a luxury the team can no longer afford. Rush threw four interceptions and led only one touchdown drive in his two starts.

DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring) was inactive and CB A.J. Terrell (groin) was out for the first of at least four games after being placed on injured reserve. While Penix was in the spotlight, another important returning player was CB Billy Bowman , who had a tackle and two passes defensed after recovering from an Achilles tendon injury.

12 — While Cameron Thomas recorded Atlanta's only sack, the Falcons had 12 pressures on Love, including four each by Thomas and Brandon Dorlus .

Stefanski described the pass rush as "outstanding" and having a big impact on Love's effectiveness.

"We love to get the sacks whenever we can, but you want to pressure quarterback and I thought he was under pressure quite a bit," Stefanski said.

The Falcons will play another prime-time game when they visit New Orleans on Monday, Oct. 5.

articles.title: The Giants’ Injury Bug Unlocks Arvell Reeses’ Perfect Role
articles.summary: Week 2 of the 2026 season is one of the darkest days in recent memory for New York Giants fans. Jaxson Dart‘s season-ending injury, along with injuries to Al...
articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 season is one of the darkest days in recent memory for New York Giants fans.

Jaxson Dart 's season-ending injury, along with injuries to All-Pros Brian Burns and Andrew Thomas , leaves the rest of the season feeling hopeless.

However, there is a silver lining in the injury plague: giving Arvell Reese the freedom to develop everywhere on the field.

Burns' Absence Opens the Door for Reese on the Edge

Burns is bound to miss time with his ankle injury, creating a void on the edge.

Though Reese has had a solid start to his rookie campaign at linebacker, his edge-rush potential is too good to leave untested. He dominated up front at Ohio State, logging 8.0 sacks and 23 pressures in just 104 pass-rush snaps in his final season with the Buckeyes.

Reese has shown his pass-rush ability in the NFL as a blitzer, too. He's already at two pressures on just six pass rushes. His strength and size make him a force anywhere on the line, but now is the time to test him on the edge in a real role.

Reese has held up well enough to keep playing in the middle of the field, but with the Giants' contention chances slim, Burns' injury is a perfect opportunity to see how his rushing translates at the pro level.

If he plays well there too, New York will have unlocked one of the league's most versatile defenders.

A Derailed Season Gives the Giants Room to Let Reese Grow

Reese has translated his physicality well to the NFL, but his coverage still needs significant work. Quick reactions in space will be the biggest area for growth as he shifts full-time to middle linebacker.

Reese has struggled to lock onto matchups, and his indecisiveness has cost New York at times . After a strong Week 1, there may have been urgency to mask the issue. The Dart injury changes everything.

Now, though, the G-Men can view this more as a season of experimenting with their building blocks.

Before, they may have felt they needed to switch Reese into easier coverage matchups to hide his coverage struggles temporarily. Now, the Giants will feel comfortable putting Reese anywhere this season. They can line him up anywhere in the front seven and see what works best once the team is fully healthy.

From there, the New York Giants' defense can be transformative, lining Arvell Reese anywhere up front and knowing he can hold his own at multiple spots.
